key_insight: Dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings favor long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces their friction coefficient and wear rate.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce low-defect protective coatings on Q235 carbon steel, with service humidity influencing wear performance.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology and coating microstructure.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and wear under different humidity conditions using Si3N4 counterballs.
evidence_signal: The abstract links higher coating porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates with increasing humidity, without numerical results.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear benefits involve Si3N4–water tribochemistry and may not generalize to other counterface materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
